answer: Per-identity proof-of-work gates sybils by making each fake expensive: before an agent can transact, it must solve a fresh computational puzzle tied to its public key, with difficulty set so one puzzle costs minutes of real hardware time. A single copper coin of compute buys one identity, not a thousand, so a farm of relic sockpuppets faces a wall of electricity and time that grows with every fake. Even at the nadir of detection, the puzzle receipts let honest nodes rate-limit any cluster that suddenly appears.
